Desc: -50A Id, -60V Vds, TrenchFET P-Channel Power MOSFET, 15mOhm Ron, 165nC Qg, -55 to 150 °C, TO-252-2
Quote: MPN set to the Vishay base part number, consistent with this board's treatment of SS54 and 1N4148W. Packaging/RoHS suffix (-E3 / -GE3 style) is a distributor choice at order time.
Note: REV 2.0: reverse-polarity protection for the whole board, replacing D4 (SS54), which was removed as redundant. ORIENTATION IS A SILENT FAILURE MODE: drain (pad 2, the tab) faces the input +12V_RAW; source (pad 3) faces +12V. The body diode must conduct input->output. Reversed, the board powers up and runs normally and the defect only appears the day J2 is miswired - which is the only day it matters. Verify on a current-limited bench supply before the board goes in the vehicle: correct polarity shows a near-zero drop across Q1, reversed draws nothing. Rds(on) 15 mOhm at Vgs=-10V gives 38 mV and 0.11W at the 3A budget, against the SS54 it replaces at ~500 mV and ~1.5W - which is the whole point, since S3.7.4 moved the Pi tap upstream precisely to keep a diode drop out of a supply that must survive cranking sag. -60V clears D1 SMBJ24A max clamping voltage of 38.9V. CONFIRM Vgs(max) FROM THE PART DATASHEET before ordering - the selection guide does not list it and D3 was sized assuming the usual +/-20V.

K-line commander pull-up high-side switch. Connects/disconnects R5 (1k) from +12V, replacing the J5 jumper so the mode is software-selectable instead of needing the HAT unstacked from under the dash. GPIO24 high -> Q3 conducts -> R13/R14 divide +12V to 1.09V at this gate -> Vgs = -10.9V, inside the +/-20V limit. GPIO low OR high-Z -> R13 holds the gate at +12V -> Vgs = 0 -> off. So passive sniff mode is the safe default and a Pi that is off, booting or crashed cannot perturb a scan-tool session. Rds(on) ~10 ohm is a 1% error on a 1k pull-up. Body diode conducts D->S, i.e. away from the bus, so with Q2 off the pull-up is genuinely disconnected.

Level-shifts GPIO24 up to Q2's gate; sinks only ~109 uA. Logic-level part, fully on at Vgs = 3.3V. R15 pulls its gate down so it is off whenever the Pi is not actively driving GPIO24 high - that is what makes sniff mode the default.
